pr_title: Allow MinGW build to use BCryptGenRandom like MS VC build [1.1.1]
pr_body:
We use `LoadLibraryA` to load bcrypt.dll from Windows System32 directory and retrieve the function pointer to `BCryptGenRandom` in order to call it dynamically at runtime.
We also use `GetModuleHandleExA` to pin bcrypt.dll in the process memory in order to replicate the previous behavior where bcrypt.dll was linked against explicitly at link time as dependency. This also avoid performance penalty of loading bcrypt.dll each time.

Fixes #13878
pr_comments: You're targeting the 1.1.1-stable branch. I assume that the master branch will also need this. Our flow is to merge things in master first. If possible, and we think this should get fixed in 1.1.1, we'll apply this in 1.1.1 too. If it doesn't apply cleanly, it will need a separate pull request.

Thank you for the feedback.
Indeed, the master branch contains the same implementation and so the same modification applies to it.
I will prepare a new pull request targeting the master branch.

Related to  #11757, similar to #8916.
@idrassi : please take a look at https://www.openssl.org/policies/cla.html

@FdaSilvaYY Thank you for the links.

I checked the pull request #8916 and it has 3 main differences:

1. it limits the dynamic loading to MS Visual Studio builds.
2. it doesn't load bcrypt.dll using full path which can open the door to dll hijacking attacks since bcrypt.dll is not part of the KnownDLLs list.
3. it doesn't pin bcrypt.dll into the process memory in order to protect it from being unloaded during the course of the process execution.

Concerning the CLA, I have sent yesterday an email to the legal address with the signed PDF document.

EDIT: #8916 makes use of  `RUN_ONCE` and `DEFINE_RUN_ONCE_STATIC` macros, which is more efficient than calling Windows `GetModuleHandleExA`/`GetProcAddress` especially that we are pinning bcrypt.dll. I will update the pull request to use this approach and also create a equivalent new pull request for master.

issue_context.title: MinGW build doesn't use BCryptGenRandom like MS VC build and it is limited to depricated CryptGenRandom
issue_context.body:
Applies to both master and 1.1.1-stable branch.

in `crypto/rand/rand_win.c`, the code to use the recommended `BCryptGenRandom`  from bcrypt.dll is limited to the use of Visual Studio 2008 and newer through a check on the proprietary `_MSC_VER` define.

This means that if OpenSSL is built using MinGW, the random generator falls back to using the deprecated CryptGenRandom function even on new Windows versions like Windows 10 although bcrypt.dll is present on these new systems and BCryptGenRandom can be called at runtime.

I believe this was done this way because MinGW doesn't provide bcrypt.h header file but this is the wrong approach since `BCryptGenRandom` function can be called at runtime by loading bcrypt.dll and retrieving the function pointer dynamically from it using GetProcAddress.

review_comments: This is to handle the case of `GetSystemDirectoryA` call failing. This should never happen of course. As an alternative we can also consider that the system is broken in such event and simply not use bcrypt.dll instead of using the hard-coded path.
